Latin word

prīdiē

adverb; prīdiē quam with a clause, prīdiē ejus diēī, or prīdiē with the accusative of a date

the day before

In this lexicon

  • the day before

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 5.11.6: prīdiē quam ego Athēnās vēnī (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 1.47: prīdiē ejus diēī (Lewis & Short); Traupman 86; Traupman 300

  • prīdiē nātālem Chrīstī: Christmas Eve

    modern

  • prīdiē Kalendās Jānuāriās: New Year’s Eve

    classical

Examples

  • nēmō nostrum est īdem māne quī fuit prīdiē

    none of us is the same in the morning as he was the day beforeSen. Ep. 58.22

    In the entry for the day before

  • prīdiē quam abīret

    on the day before he leftTraupman 86

    In the entry for the day before
